USB package (14 Oct 2026; distribution only, the module source and version are unchanged): loads over USB on the Modwerk beta base as an independent machine package. Its chooser row, page and renderer go through the base’s machine table, and its 909/808 DSP engine is resident in the base on both cores. The base admits this exact package through a trust row built into it; its renderer writes only under the base’s write lease and renders silent until the base has reset and enabled the engine, whose reset restores its authored tables. It needs that exact base; with an older base the site asks for a base update first. Its compiled bytes that coincide with stock are copied at install from bytes the base checks against its running stock, so the package carries no stock bytes.

Lower Mini Verb's DSP cost without changing its sound: two coefficient reloads whose register already held the value are removed from the sample loop. The modeled loop cost falls from 415 to 411 cycles per sample. The Octatrack USB loader charges 7/4 of that, 720 chip cycles (415 would be 727), which fits the smaller DSP core's 726-cycle allowance for one module beside seven stock effects.

Integrate the module into source packages and native/browser composition; retain the contributor's MKII functional hardware report. Missing current hardware timing and stress evidence is owner-approved.

Runtime package only: one package now works with or without Sidechain Compressor. Instead of a separate SC_KEY build, the package asks the base's ev_mute_keep event once per frame in OTFX, OTFX-T and DT-T which tracks another installed module reads while muted (a side-chain KEY), and mutes those as stock does, as the SC_KEY build did for Sidechain's KEY. With no module answering it behaves exactly as the plain build. Mute Modes no longer names Sidechain; the module that owns the KEY answers.

Runtime package only: MUTE MODE survives a power cycle on a Modwerk base. The loader installs the kept module after boot has already restored the PERSONALIZE settings, so on the first UI tick after an install the package takes MUTE MODE from its battery copy, as the native build's widened boot restore does.

Limits: needs a base built with site events that raises ev_mute_keep; the loader gives the package that base's entry at install. Until Sidechain Compressor answers ev_mute_keep, a muted Sidechain KEY track goes silent in the soft modes beside it. Native octabam builds are byte-identical to the author's references (plain, SC_KEY and menu). Emulator evidence only, with synthetic mute/mode words, DSP records and a stand-in provider; physical audio, power-cycle persistence and current-build hardware remain untested. Prepared, not released.

USB package (14 Oct 2026; distribution only, the module source and version are unchanged): published. The Modwerk base admits its grown PERSONALIZE tables only through a reviewed table declaration bound to this exact package (SHA-256 c35b154d...), built into the base, and the base checks every table word it copies against its running stock. The emulator evidence above ran an earlier packet (a48be767...); this package has emulator and host build checks only, and the table/menu pointer lifetime on hardware is unverified. The owner waived hardware evidence for this exact version's USB package for the beta.

Runtime package only: on a Modwerk base that owns the fresh-voice-bind site 0x40006820 (sdk/machines/octatrack/events.json), the fresh-bind gate is an ev_voice_bind subscriber (order 50) instead of a raw detour, so it installs beside POLY8 and any other subscriber. The subscriber runs the same fresh_bind code; only its two exits answer the base instead of jumping into stock. Native octabam builds, plain and SC_KEY, assemble byte-identical to the author's references.

Limits: needs a base built with site events; older bases refuse this package, and Undo keeps 0.1.0-experimental for them. The other five detours, including mt_trig at 0x40006844, stay as they were. Emulator evidence only (synthetic mute/mode words); physical audio and current-build hardware remain untested.
Add OT, OTFX, OTFX-T and DT-T mute behavior through PROJECT > SYSTEM > PERSONALIZE, retaining the MKII LED BRIGHTNESS row.

Automatically select the authored SC_KEY variant beside Sidechain Compressor. Native execution covers mute/solo masks, cue preservation, settings and sidechain paths. Physical audio and current-build hardware remain untested and owner-approved where absent.
Presentation: illustrate the four mute behaviors using the library's shared signal artwork, grid, palette and typography.
Add recorder-buffer voice and counter fixes, END-1 hold behavior and fixed-RLEN spacing correction to the selectable shared builder.

Correct the upstream arm/q phase drift: all 13,279 long-run cases, 555,008 early cases and 1,244,352 fractional-tempo/uint32-boundary cases pass. Fixed RLEN 1–64 at 30–300 BPM is supported; other ranges retain stock length.

Guard all eight detours and relocate eleven pool-base literals with the sample arena. Consecutive-arm arithmetic is tested; physical audio continuity, non-consecutive arm history and current-build hardware remain unmeasured. The owner approved missing hardware evidence.
Presentation: show repeating recorder segments and tempo boundaries using the library's shared signal artwork, grid, palette and typography.

Protect stock T3 inter-core mailbox and T7 parameter staging data by keeping the first 72 virtual ring words in safe per-instance X state. Preserve stock track state, full stereo delay range, smoothing, controls and saved parameter layout.

Losslessly pack all original sine values into 256 DSP words and reduce code/table storage from 1,425 to 795 words per core. Air Chorus now combines with E-Verb and Analog BD, including more DSP companions; larger selections remain limited by available program space.

The shared-data corruption is reproduced and checked in software. The tester still reported T3 clicking in 0.1.1; whether this update fixes that audible hardware symptom remains unverified. Current hardware timing, multi-instance audio and Part/project/reboot persistence are owner-waived for this exact beta source/version.
Documentation/media-only: add an offline audio preview rendered through 0.1.2-experimental, with sample credits, settings and provenance; firmware is unchanged.

Beta release for beta testers: reduces measured DSP work by 35.80% with the original full stereo delay range, smoothing and control meanings retained. Thirty recorded comparison fixtures are bit-identical to 0.1.0.

Targets the reported multi-instance clicking by reducing DSP load. The T3/T4 emulator reproduction did not reproduce the hardware symptom, so this is a mitigation pending beta hardware results, not a confirmed clicking fix.

FX2 only. Current hardware testing is owner-waived for this exact version/source; physical timing, multi-instance audio and Part/project/reboot persistence remain unverified. Existing control values and saved parameter layout are unchanged.
First release of Chris Johnson’s MIT-licensed Airwindows Chorus as an Octatrack FX2 module; original source and full attribution retained.
Smooth SPD, RNG and MIX per sample, preserve the original air compensation and three-point delay read, and initialize dirty rings without a long synchronous clear.

Owner reports 50 minutes of successful MKII use with several instances and full knob sweeps on the first image. Fresh hardware testing of the bounded-init image is waived; eight-track timing, locks/scenes/LFOs and physical persistence remain unverified.
Delay precision is approximately 16 bits; extreme modulation retains pitch and aliasing artifacts.

Runtime package only: on a Modwerk base that owns 0x40004100 and 0x40006820 (sdk/machines/octatrack/events.json), POLY8 subscribes instead of patching them: ev_play_increment (order 20) takes POLY tracks, ev_voice_bind (order 20) handles resets its renderer causes, ev_voice_bind_run discards a track's extension voices when a reset runs. Repitch and Mute Modes then install beside it without POLY8 linking their code.
The subscribers are appended to polyphony.s under MODWERK_EVENTS with absolute addressing, so no existing PC-relative displacement moves; native octabam builds assemble byte-identical.

Limits: needs a base built with site events; older bases refuse this package, and Undo keeps 0.2.7-experimental for them. Emulator evidence only (synthetic renderer flags and register state); current-build hardware, chip worst-case timing and complete memory bounds remain unqualified.

USB package (14 Oct 2026; distribution only, the module source and version are unchanged): loads over USB as one independent package beside every other module, on a Modwerk base built with site events. Media-only: replace the POLY8 thumbnail with an original eight-voice sample diagram using the library’s shared grid, lavender signal palette and typography.

Release the previous sequenced chord once before the next native sample trig, so finite AMP REL can end its tails even with HOLD INF. Preserve all notes in the new chord and independently owned panel/MIDI notes. Related to https://github.com/repeat98/modwerk/issues/447.
Keep finite HOLD, intentional REL INF sustain and native STOP behavior. Recorded key-up timing remains unsupported; the final chord with HOLD INF sustains until another trig or STOP.

The owner approved this scoped experimental release with current-build hardware, chip worst-case timing and complete memory qualification waived. Native playback tests pass; physical MKI confirmation remains pending. Keep issue 447 open until the exact published download is verified on the affected unit.
Combine POLY8 with Repitch, Mute Modes and Scale Quantizer through guarded shared hooks; other configurations retain their original build paths.
Add a bounded native chooser for POLY8, Analog BD, VECTOR and FM Synth together. Each machine retains its own saved Part marker, controls and playback engine.
Use FM Synth’s bundled signature-aware quantizer when both quantizers are selected; preserve its complete helper-pointer ABI and refuse changed or unknown overlapping claims.

Keep the pitch cache within signed ColdFire PC-relative addressing range; prevent silent assembler displacement wrap from overwriting preceding companion-machine code. Add a firmware-free check of all 121 compiled local PC-relative addresses.
Restore NO dismissal of the one-POLY8 refusal using stock’s modal input layer while retaining its automatic native timeout.
Retain eight POLY8 voices, one POLY8 assignment per Part, LOOP OFF on new assignments and fixed 1/8 gain. Existing DSP memory and menu-space limits still apply; Octakit remains incompatible.

Load the shared chooser initialization flag explicitly instead of relying on uncleared BSS. Nonzero RAM reproduces an odd widget target at the T07/T08 boot-failure call; add a compiled-section startup-state gate. T07/T08 are withdrawn; the owner reports corrected T09 works on MKII, without a separate test checklist.

The owner reports exact T10 “works like a charm” on MKII and approves this scoped experimental release. Separately reported recording/load/persistence cases, chip worst-case timing and complete memory bounds remain unverified; combined-machine results are emulator evidence.

Preserve current VECTOR 0.2.4 packed-setting validation through the shared machine bridge; a sanitizer regression covers all 256 mixed AB/FM/VECTOR signature masks. The exact T10 selection flow is checked against stock FLEX/STATIC controls and the earlier T09 regression.
Match FLEX/STATIC selection: POLY8 assignment and reselection stay on the current page. Double-TRACK opens FLEX samples; LEFT/RIGHT and sample confirmation remain available.
Publish as POLY8, including the machine chooser and refusal dialog, while preserving PL/1 saved-Part identity.
First public experimental release: eight shared sample voices, one POLY per Part, independent envelopes and fixed 1/8 gain.
POLY8T06 preserves an existing POLY track’s LOOP setting when reselecting the machine; newly assigned tracks still default to OFF.
Returning LEFT from POLY’s sample slots restores the POLY machine cursor and title; RIGHT opens FLEX samples again.

Reduce ColdFire interpolation and held-voice mixing instructions without changing eight-voice admission, envelopes or fixed 1/8 gain. Skip redundant peak measurement while the limiter is at unity, retaining defensive output saturation.
Retain the original DSP payloads and existing core logger. Native load comparisons and panel flows are emulator evidence; physical CPU deadlines, recording and reboot qualification remain pending.
Panel recording supports at most four notes spanning eleven semitones; recorded duration follows AMP HOLD. Extended MIDI recording and grid root editing remain incomplete.

POLY8T05 private test preserves both original 1.40C DSP uploads byte for byte and bypasses the SDK automatic stock-effect dynamic loader. The build refuses DSP drift or an implicit loader. This isolates a dependency candidate after T04 hardware logs showed no sample-render entries; it is not a confirmed hardware fix.
Add bounded counts for native command-consumer and AMP-builder calls, including stock tracks. The existing core logger snapshots them outside audio callbacks.

Retain eight voices, one POLY per Part, fixed 1/8 gain, LOOP OFF for new assignments, scratch bounds, timed modal and marker persistence correction. Physical recording, reboot and transport/audio results remain unverified on this version.

POLY8T04 private diagnostic candidate includes the existing core OCTAMOD.LOG logger and bounded once-per-second POLY transport, render/fetch, key/record, voice and modal snapshots. No filesystem work occurs in audio or UI callbacks.

Reserve scratch buffers for all 32 physical selectors while retaining the eight-active-voice cap; sparse extension indices can no longer address beyond scratch storage. This is a defensive bounds correction, not a confirmed cause of the MKII stall.
Keep the one-POLY refusal modal but automatically dismiss it after 120 native UI ticks, so an overlooked dialog cannot indefinitely capture panel input.
Retain fixed 1/8 gain, LOOP OFF for new assignments and the battery-RAM marker copy correction. MKII recording and transport/audio failures remain open until this exact build is tested on hardware.
Retain the eight-head cap and pitch-work budget; allow one POLY assignment per Part. Refuse a second machine before any settings/sample writes, with a native NO-dismissed modal.
Apply fixed 1/8 (-18.06 dB) gain in both the single-voice fast path and envelope-weighted mix; leave headroom for eight coherent full-scale voices without voice-count pumping.
Correct the PL/1 marker copy into battery RAM by staging its reads before writes; normal restart can retain POLY identity.

Fresh-assignment native REC+PLAY succeeds, but the previous image also succeeds in that emulator path. The reported MKII recording failure remains unresolved on hardware; do not claim this gain/persistence update fixes it. LOOP OFF default remains unchanged.
Restore the native panel recorder for up to four-note chords spanning eleven semitones; consume encoded roots before normal PTCH locks, retaining native SAMPLE locks.
Limit this hardware test to eight shared voices with pitch-weighted admission; steal released tails before held notes and ignore duplicate held-key presses.
New POLY assignments default to LOOP OFF. Browser confirmations and existing saved LOOP choices retain their value.
Recorded duration follows AMP HOLD; wider chords, extended MIDI recording, grid root editing and physical MKII deadlines remain unqualified.
32 active POLY voices share one global pool; one track can use all free voices.
Independent preallocated AMP envelopes with shared per-track filters and FX.
PTCH tuning is independent of chromatic and MIDI notes, with ten panel octave positions and dedicated-route MIDI 0–127.
Selecting POLY opens native FLEX samples directly; STATIC is excluded.
Hardware deadlines, broad lifecycle combinations, note recording and public packaging remain unqualified.

Holding FUNC while turning SIZE, DCY, ABSB or SPD now steps through 0, the centre (64) and 127, as MIX and DPTH already did and as on the stock reverbs' MIX. In 0.1.0 those four knobs jumped only between 0 and 127, an editor inherited from the stock reverb that E-Verb's page is cloned from (#438).

Plain turns and every stored value are unchanged: only four editor words in E-Verb's FX2 descriptor change. The DSP code and memory are byte-identical to 0.1.0, so the sound and cycle cost are unchanged, and the knob values a project stores mean the same.

The six main-page controls support locks, LFOs, scenes and MIDI CC; SETUP controls are per Part. MIX 0 is exact dry passthrough.
Uses the shared native/browser builder; alone, replaces Spring Rev and Dark Rev while preserving Plate Rev and other stock effects.

Owner reports working MKII sound, two distinct simultaneous T1/T5 instances, Part/project save/reload and physical reboot on exact EVRB01T01. Full-load silicon timing and broader hardware modulation/recovery coverage remain unverified.

First release: the CUE CFG box, titled OUT CFG with the module, gains MATRIX, which makes the headphone jack a third assignable output beside MAIN and CUE. CUE + LEVEL picks each track's outputs (any combination of MAIN, CUE and PHONES, or one of six mono jacks); the routing lives in the Part. MIX becomes the PHONES level, and the metronome also plays on PHONES.
Switching to or from MATRIX converts every Part's LEVEL and cue bytes by documented rules, and switching into NORMAL also sets the project's cue settings.
Builds with the stock DSP code built in: its core-0 code takes a given-up stock reverb's space (SPRING REV first), which leaves the FX2 menu. It cannot be combined with Analog BD yet.
Author's functional MKII report (7–9 Oct 2026) covers routing, levels, everyday flows, saving and power; no timed stress run or chip timing.

First Modwerk release for Digitakt I OS 1.53 and 1.54, on Core 2.1. Use the native retrig menu on MIDI tracks A–H. Repeated notes follow the Digitakt sequencer, including chords, retrig rate, finite length and velocity changes.

First Modwerk release for Digitakt I OS 1.53 and 1.54, on Core 2.1. Generate rhythms from two pulse generators on each audio or MIDI track. Rotate either generator, rotate the whole result and combine them with OR, XOR, AND or SUB.

First Modwerk release for Digitakt I OS 1.53 and 1.54, on Core 2.1. RAM-R1 records a temporary mono take from the master mix or inputs when triggered. RAM-P1 plays that shared take using the native sample controls.

RAM-P1 now plays a take at the level it was recorded at. 1.1.1 played takes about 17 dB quieter, because a take recorded from MAIN passed through a second voice gain on playback. Existing projects will play RAM-P1 louder.

Takes are normalized to full scale when recording ends, so BR (bit reduction) on RAM-P1 sounds as it does on a normal sample instead of much stronger. The pass runs in the audio interrupt from both ends of the take; a trig with STRT inside a long take in the second after it ends can briefly play quieter.
Written takes are pushed from the CPU cache so the sample DMA always reads the new take, including after a Sample Snap and Crossfade commit.
